chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibn Mahbub, from Hammad ibn Ziyad, from Sulayman ibn Khalid, who said:
I asked Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a slave jointly owned by two partners, one of whom emancipated his share; then the slave committed one of the hudud of Allah.

He عليه السلام said: "If, when half of the slave was emancipated, he had been appraised so that the one who emancipated him would be charged his value, then half of him is free, and he is given half the hadd of a free person and half the hadd of a slave. But if he had not been appraised, then this is a slave, and he is given the hadd of a slave."

key_terms.أَعْتَقَ: emancipated; freed a share of the slave
key_terms.حَدَّ ٱلْعَبْدِ: the prescribed punishment applicable to a slave
key_terms.حَدِّ ٱلْحُرِّ: the prescribed punishment applicable to a free person
key_terms.حُرٌّ: free; legally no longer enslaved in full
key_terms.شَرِيكَيْنِ: two partners who jointly own the slave
key_terms.عَبْدٍ: a slave; the legal subject discussed in the ruling

ai.seo_question: How is the hadd punishment applied to a partially emancipated slave in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a jointly owned slave whose one share was emancipated and who then became liable for a hadd punishment. The ruling distinguishes between whether the slave had been formally appraised for compensation at the time of partial emancipation, affecting whether he is treated as partially free or fully enslaved for the purpose of the hadd.
